Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])

In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.dummy import DummyClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV

X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

# refit=False: no refit timing should be produced on a fresh search.
search = GridSearchCV(DummyClassifier(), {'strategy': ['most_frequent', 'uniform']},
                      cv=2, refit=False).fit(X, y)
assert not hasattr(search, 'refit_time_')
assert not hasattr(search, 'best_estimator_')

# Multimetric string refit: still a measured nonnegative duration.
search = GridSearchCV(DummyClassifier(), {'strategy': ['most_frequent']}, cv=2,
                      scoring={'acc': 'accuracy', 'f1': 'f1_macro'},
                      refit='acc').fit(X, y)
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float) and search.refit_time_ >= 0
assert search.best_estimator_ is not None

# RandomizedSearchCV shares BaseSearchCV.fit.
search = RandomizedSearchCV(DummyClassifier(), {'strategy': ['most_frequent', 'uniform']},
                            n_iter=2, cv=2, random_state=0).fit(X, y)
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float) and search.refit_time_ >= 0

# Unsupervised estimator: the no-y refit path is timed too.
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
search = GridSearchCV(KMeans(random_state=0), {'n_clusters': [2, 3]}, cv=2).fit(X)
assert isinstance(search.refit_time_, float) and search.refit_time_ >= 0
print('edge cases OK:', search.refit_time_)
